notes: Fifth sweep (2026-10-22-d, head ba24972, uncommitted false in every result.json): five baseline runs (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), all rc 0, each model_id matching its tier. No transcript has a Skill tool call (each session used only Read on the input file, Write and Bash; opus-1 ran the file 15 times), and reads is empty in all five, as the prompt's last line requires; skills_listed is 29. Expected reads (now ex_unit.md and processes.md) is therefore unmet in every run, as expected for baseline. Every run's test-writing-input.ex is identical to evals/cases/test-writing-input.ex.

Changes since 3e3581d (git diff 3e3581d -- idiomatic-elixir/): references/testing.md is renamed to references/ex_unit.md (the case's Expected reads line follows); in ex_unit.md only "Assert with patterns" changed; in SKILL.md a "Formatting" bullet was added under "How to use this skill", "Before you finish" step 1 was reworded, and "Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call" and "Use `do:` for a one-expression body and `do ... end` for anything else" were rewritten. The other seven graded rules are unchanged and graded to the standard of sweeps/2026-10-22-c/grades/test-writing-*.json.

Changed rule: "Assert with patterns" (references/ex_unit.md). The == order sentence now reads: "The value under test goes on the left of `==` and the expected value on the right, whether it is the call itself or a result bound a line earlier". No run puts an expected value on the left of ==, whether against a call or a bound result (e.g. opus-1 line 125: assert sync(server) == []; sonnet-2 line 57: assert Subscriptions.subscribe(server, "news", "a@example.com") == :ok; haiku-2 line 66 and sonnet-2 line 47: assert Process.whereis(...) == pid, a held value on the right), so that sentence decides no verdict. The bare-match sentence (unchanged since 2026-10-22-c) decides all three violations, counted as in 2026-10-22-c (a literal, tuple, list or map on the left, without assert, inside a test block; not plain-variable bindings, receive clauses such as sonnet-1 line 49, or matches in helpers): opus-1 22, all :ok = calls (lines 75, 76, 85, 93, 94, 96, 103, 104, 106, 113, 114, 116, 130, 131, 133, 145, 146, 147, 148, 158, 159, 162); haiku-1 0; haiku-2 22 (lines 68, 90, 104, 105, 106, 114, 122, 131, 132, 133, 143, 144, 165, 174, 185, 186, 197, 198, 199, 208, 209, 221); sonnet-1 34 (lines 85, 86, 87, 93, 94, 107, 108, 114, 115, 121, 122, 123, 124, 132, 133, 134, 142, 150, 151, 152, 159, 160, 161, 172, 183, 184, 195, 196, 197, 207, 220, 221, 226, 236); sonnet-2 0. Rule result: 3 of 5 (opus-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1), as 3 of 5 in 2026-10-22-c. No run uses elem/2 or binds a held value and compares it with == afterwards.

Changed rule outside the list: "Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call" (SKILL.md). The sentence that decides sonnet-1 line 68 is "Unless a call's result is bound to a name, each of its arguments is a name or a short literal: a map, struct or keyword list that would span several lines is built first under a name ... That holds whether the result is passed on, matched against, nested in another call or discarded." sonnet-1 line 68 discards the result of start_supervised!(%{id: name, start: {...}}) and mix format spreads that map over four lines, so it is recorded in other_violations. haiku-2 line 64 (pid = start_supervised!(Supervisor.child_spec(...))) and sonnet-1 line 26 (server = start_supervised!(...)) bind the result, which the new text allows ("A call whose result is bound to a name may take its options inline"). The changed "Use `do:`" rule decides nothing here: every do: in the five files is a one-expression private helper on its head's line (opus-1 lines 25, 42; haiku-2 line 32; sonnet-1 line 41; sonnet-2 line 36). The reworded "Before you finish" step 1 still requires mix format on each changed file, so unformatted files are recorded under it as before.

"Group tests by function and name them by behaviour" (unchanged). Describe blocks: "subscribe/3 and subscribers/2" in opus-1 (line 59), sonnet-1 (line 74) and sonnet-2 (line 51); haiku-1 and haiku-2 split subscribe/3 and subscribers/2; every run's "when a subscribed process exits" names a shared condition, clean. Test names violating the test-name sentence: haiku-2 line 84 "returns :ok"; sonnet-1 line 102 "returns :ok immediately"; sonnet-2 line 56 "subscribe returns :ok" and line 86 "returns :ok immediately". Not counted, as in earlier grades: "requires the :mailer option" (opus-1 line 45), "requires a mailer" (sonnet-1 line 61), "fails to start without a :mailer" (haiku-2 line 74), "raises when the mailer option is missing" (sonnet-2 line 39), "does nothing for/when ..." (opus-1 123, haiku-1 114, haiku-2 153, sonnet-1 141, sonnet-2 125), "leaves the server running" (haiku-2 219), "subscribing returns :ok and records the subscriber" (sonnet-1 line 79, which names the effect too), "exits with a non-normal reason are handled too" (sonnet-2 line 207, borderline). opus-1's other names: "registers under the given name", "returns an empty list for a topic without subscribers", "lists subscribers most recent first", "keeps topics separate", "sends a notification to subscribed processes", "mails subscribed email addresses", "notifies processes and email addresses on the same topic", "only notifies subscribers of the published topic", "keeps notifying when the mailer returns an error", "it is removed from every topic", "it is no longer notified and the server keeps publishing". haiku-1's: "adds a pid to the subscribers of a topic", "adds an email address to the subscribers of a topic", "keeps topics independent", "uses the default name when none is given", "lists the most recent subscriber first", "returns an empty list for a topic without subscribers", "sends a notification to a subscribed pid", "mails an email subscriber", "notifies every subscriber of the topic", "does not notify subscribers of other topics", and five "removes ..."/"keeps ..."/"still notifies ..." exit tests. Rule result: 4 of 5 (haiku-1 clean), from 5 of 5 in 2026-10-22-c.

"Wait for messages, not for time" (unchanged; the :DOWN reason sentence, "Match the reason too, `:normal`, `:shutdown` or the one the test caused: a `_` there lets a crash for another reason pass", graded as in 2026-10-22-c, which counted a helper's _ as a violation; _reason is counted the same as _). Every :DOWN pattern: opus-1 line 174 _ (helper stop/1, after send(pid, :stop)); haiku-1 line 225 _reason (helper wait_for_exit/1, after :stop or :kill); haiku-2 line 59 _reason (helper stop_and_wait/1), line 179 :killed; sonnet-1 line 57 _ (helper stop_and_wait/1), line 211 :boom, line 234 _; sonnet-2 lines 162 and 226 _. Process.sleep polling after exits: haiku-1 (line 236), haiku-2 (line 43), sonnet-2 (line 255). opus-1 and sonnet-1 have no Process.sleep and follow each :DOWN with a synchronous call, so they violate only the reason sentence. Rule result: 5 of 5, from 4 of 5 in 2026-10-22-c (where opus-1 matched :killed and was clean). Single assert Process.alive?(server) checks (opus-1 line 137, haiku-1 lines 120 and 190, haiku-2 line 226, sonnet-1 lines 146 and 215, sonnet-2 lines 130, 204, 219) are not polling and are not counted.

"Run tests concurrently unless they share global state" (unchanged): violated in 4 of 5. haiku-1 (line 14) runs async: false because of Application.put_env (line 20), haiku-2 (line 4) and sonnet-2 (line 15) because of their own registered test process (lines 22, 21), and sonnet-1 (line 18) because of :persistent_term.put of the test pid (line 23), a global singleton like the application env. opus-1 is clean: one async: true module whose double finds the test pid as the last of the server's $ancestors (line 25), with no global state, unlike 2026-10-22-c, where it moved its email tests into an async: false module.

"Start processes with `start_supervised!/1`" (unchanged): violated in 4 of 5, each by start_link called from a test to assert the missing-mailer failure: opus-1 line 47, haiku-2 line 78, sonnet-1 line 63, sonnet-2 lines 42-43. haiku-1 is clean: unique names (line 23) and no start-failure test. Default-name starts that test that default (haiku-1 line 48, haiku-2 line 64), inside async: false modules, are not counted, as in 2026-10-22-c; opus-1 line 52 and sonnet-1 line 68 start servers under a name only that test uses. "Replace dependencies at boundaries, through behaviours" is clean in 5 of 5 (a module with @behaviour Notify.Mailer passed as :mailer). "Use setup for shared data" is clean in 4 of 5 with %{server: ...} maps matched in test heads; sonnet-2 returns {:ok, server: name, server_pid: pid} (line 24), a keyword list, graded violated as 2026-10-22-b graded the same shape ("Return data from `setup` as a map"). "Open a module with `use`, `import`, `alias`, `require`, in that order" is clean in 5 of 5: no test module has a @moduledoc, the directives open each body, haiku-2 has use / import / alias (lines 4, 6, 8) and the others use / alias.

Outside the list: opus-1 line 25 and sonnet-1 line 26 pipe a single step ("Write pipelines that start with a value and read top to bottom"; opus-1's pipe also starts with a call). haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 fail mix format --check-formatted, recorded under "Before you finish". Test support modules without @moduledoc (haiku-1 FakeMailer, haiku-2 FakeMailer, sonnet-1 Notify.TestMailer, sonnet-2 TestMailer), private helpers above the tests (opus-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2) and comments on private helpers are not counted, as in earlier grades. sonnet-1's comment at line 31 ("name: nil is not valid for GenServer") is factually wrong (opus-1 starts with name: nil) but breaks no rule. No captures or if ..., do: lines in any file.

Tests were run from copies in the scratch folder with elixir -r test-writing-input.ex subscriptions_test.exs on Elixir 1.20.4 (OTP 29), ten times each: every run passed every time with no warnings (opus-1 13 tests, haiku-1 16, haiku-2 17, sonnet-1 20, sonnet-2 22). mix format --check-formatted passes on opus-1 and fails on haiku-1 (line 183), haiku-2 (lines 64, 203), sonnet-1 (lines 26, 68, 89) and sonnet-2 (line 125), confirming format_ok in result.json.
